title: CRLR/87/2010 of PARVINDER SINGH @ PALVINDER SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 87 of 2010

Parvinder Singh @ Palvinder Singh
S/O Shri Malkeet Singh though his
Mother and natural guardian Smt Gurmeet
Kaur W/O Shri Malkeet Singh, R/O Vijay
Nagalia, Police Station-Bazpur, District
Udham Singh Nagar.

Revisionist(in Jail/observation home)
Versus
State of Uttarakhand
..............Respondent
Shri Lalit Sharma, Advocate present for the revisionist
Smt. M.A.Khan, Brief Holder, present for the State
Hon'ble Prafulla C. Pant, J.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
(2) This revision is directed against the order dated
01.05.2010, passed by Sessions Judge Udham Singh Nagar in
criminal appeal no. 42 of 2010 and order dated 15.04.2010,
passed by Juvenile Justice Board, Udham Singh Nagar.
(3) Brief facts of the case are that one F.I.R no 363 of 2009,
relating to offences punishable under sectin 147, 148, 302
I.P.C, was got registered by complainant Mahendra Singh
against accused Ravindra Singh, Malkeet Singh, Tajendra
Singh, Harkamal Singh and Palvindra Singh. Out of the five
present revisionist is accused Palvindra Singh. In the First

2
Information Report, it is alleged that on 05.11.2009 at about
8.p.m the aforesaid five accused formed an unlawful assembly
and armed with Sword, PATAL(heavy sharp edged weapon)
SARIA (iron rode) and iron chain, they assaulted
complainant's brother. The injured (complainant's brother)
was taken to hospital at Bazpur from where when being taken
to Haldwani for better medical treatment, he succumbed to
the injuries on the way.
(4) Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted that the
revisionist Parvinder Singh @ Palvinder Singh has been
declared juvenile by the Juvenile Justice Board. Learned
counsel for the State concedes this fact. However, the
Juvenile Justice Board rejected the bail application of the
revisionist on the ground that the revisionist may get the
company of the criminals if released on bail. The appellate
court (Sessions Judge Udham Singh Nagar) also dismissed the
appeal against the order passed by the Juvenile Justice Board
on 15.04.2010 on the same ground, taking shelter of exception
provided in section 12 of Juvenile Justice Act, 2000.
(5) On behalf of the revisionist it is submitted that
revisionist's father who is said to have been involved in the
crime is in jail. It is the mother of the Juvenile who is
seeking bail for the revisionist, as such the apprehension
expressed by the Juvenile Justice Board and the Sessions
Judge Udham Singh Nagar, is unfounded.

3
(6) The revisionist who is a Juvenile is in custody for last
more than six months. No specific role is assigned to him in
the First Information Report.
(7) In the above circumstances, this revision is allowed. The
impugned order dated 15.04.2010 passed by Juvenile Justice
Board Udham Singh Nagar and order dated 01.05.2010 passed
by Sessions Judge, Udham Singh Nagar, in criminal appeal
no. 42 of 2010 are set aside. The revisionist Parvinder Singh
@ Palvinder Singh shall be released on bail on furnishing
personal bond by his mother Gurmeet kaur, and two sureties
each of like amount, to the satisfaction of the Juvenile Justice
Board, Udham Singh Nagar.
 (Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
Dt.19.5.2010
N.P
